The images below illustrate the signifi cant progress being made on the Sustainable Transport Bridge substructure in 
recent months.  Four concrete piers, the northern and southern bridge abutments are all now visible above the 
waterline.  The temporary bridge supports are being installed in the water which will assist with the installation of the 
bridge deck. The fabrication of the steel bridge deck superstructure is complete, and the mechanical and electrical 
components are currently being installed in Belgium. This process also involves global supply chains for the precision 
engineering of mechanical components that will control the lifting and closing of the opening spans of the bridge. The 
fabrication of the steel bridge deck superstructure is complete, and the mechanical and electrical components are 
currently being installed in Belgium.    
The transportation of the individual fabricated deck sections to Waterford is itself a signifi cant engineering and logistical 
challenge. The separate deck sections weigh up to 300 tonnes, which is similar to the weight of a Boeing 747. These will 
be lifted by self-propelled platform trucks onto sea barges which will then be towed by canal from Ghent out to the North 
Sea for onward transport to Waterford. In addition, a large 900 tonne capacity fl oating sheerleg crane will also travel by 
sea from Belgium to complete the lifting and installation of the deck sections in Waterford.
The transport route via the North Sea, English Channel and Celtic Sea is prone to strong winter storms, and following an 
assessment of this risk, Victor Buyck will transport the fully fi tted out deck sections to Waterford next Spring for 
installation on site. This scheduling will not impact on the completion of the overall works programme. The towing of 
the large deck sections and fl oating crane up the River Suir and the installation on site next Spring will be a spectacular 
milestone for the project and the City

The team is currently addressing a total of 284 properties classifi ed as either derelict or potentially derelict. Recent 
weeks and months have seen a signifi cant increase in activity, with 96 properties now listed on the Derelict Sites 
Register. Initial engagement with property owners or their representatives is crucial for resolving issues related to 
dereliction and for gaining insights into the various factors contributing to the properties’ current state.  
The level of activity in the property market concerning vacant and derelict properties has notably increased. Among the 
properties we have identifi ed as derelict, several have been reintroduced to the private market voluntarily, with some 
currently at the ‘sale agreed’ or ‘to let’ stages. We are actively engaging with the new owners of these properties to 
ensure they are fully informed of their obligations under the Derelict Sites Act 1990. Additionally, the introduction of the 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant has contributed to a signifi cant rise in the number of derelict and vacant 
properties available on the market at this time.

Heritage Officer Report 
Heritage Week 2024
Decade of Commemorations
The launch of The Aftermath, a film by John Foley and funded by Waterford City and Council Commemorations 
Committee took place on Tuesday, September 10th with a very positive response. The Aftermath captures the 
memories and thoughts of Waterford people talking about their ancestors involved in the War of Independence and the 
Civil War. The documentary film looks at some of the key events and the people involved and also looks at what 
happened to those involved in the decades following the period. The film was funded through the Department of 
Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltact, Sports and Media’s Decade of Commemorations Fund.  Further screenings are 
scheduled for October 15th and November 13th. 
See www.facebook.com/johnfoleyimages for details.
Monastic Lismore Seminar
A Seminar on Monastic Lismore will take place on Saturday November 16th 10 am- 1pm in Lismore Heritage Centre. 
The seminar will explore the part played by Lismore and its surrounding region along the Blackwater Valley in the story 
of medieval Irish monasticism, communicating recent scholarly work on Irish monasticism in accessible and informal 
presentations.  The seminar builds on the recent publication of Monasticism in Ireland AD900–1250 by Waterford based 
Dr. Edel Bhreathnach. The seminar is free of charge, but pre-booking is required on Eventbrite.
Heritage Plan Grant Scheme
Projects allocated funding by the Heritage Council’s Heritage Plan Fund are progressing well. 
Shared Island Study Trip
Culture and heritage staff from Waterford City and County Council visited Mid and East Antrim on a two-day study trip 
on September 17th-18th.  The trip was funded by Creative Communities on a Shared Island, an initiative of Creative 
Ireland. The project aims to develop connections between communities in Mid and East Antrim and Waterford through a 
variety of culture and heritage projects.  The study visit included guided tours of Raceview Mill, Broughshane and 
Gracehill Village, which recently secured UNESCO World Heritage status. The theme of the project is based on 
commonalities in industrial heritage, concentrating on textiles such as the linen and cotton industries..

Biodiversity Officer
Waterford Biodiversity Action Plan – Preparation Stage
The Waterford Biodiversity Action Plan is in the development phase. This process will continue over the course of 2024 
and into early 2025.
•A presentation was made on the Biodiversity Action Plan to the Heritage Strategy Working Group on 6th Sept.  
•The Biodiversity Officer joined Climate Action Team to deliver a workshop on aspects of biodiversity for clubs 
participating in the GAA Climate Action Project with clubs present from multiple MDs.
•Joined the Climate Action Team on 28th Sept. to present on ‘Biodiversity for Communities’ at Mount Congreve event 
for Community Climate Action Fund recipients. 17 community groups including Tidy Towns, GAA clubs and residents’ 
associations present from across the county.
•The SE Regional Operational Committee for the Water Frameworks Directive met in Kilkenny on 5th September 2024. 
River restoration and community funding were amongst the topics discussed.
•Represented Waterford in the quarterly meeting of the national Biodiversity Officer Network at the Marine Institute in 
Oranmore, Galway.  Discussions were had on the need for additional attention to biodiversity in planning and mapping 
on a national level.

COMMUNITY GRANTS
1.Window 2, Community Recognition Fund 2024
Window 2 of the CRF 2024 opened on August 1st, with a deadline for receipt of applications by the 6th of September. 
During this call, 6 applications were reviewed and reviewed in line with the criteria of the fund.  3 applications will be rec-
ommended to the Department for approval by their deadline of the 30th of September.  
2.Local Enhancement Programme 2024
Waterford City & County Council received €153,405.12 and a further €31,824.28 specifically for Women’s Groups.  The 
Council received 227 applications of which 37 were ineligible and 190 were successful (164 under the Main fund and 26 
under the Women’s Groups fund).  
Grant monies must be expended and drawn down from the Council.  As of the 30th of September 2024, 100 groups had 
submitted receipts to Council.   
3.2024 Dormant Accounts Fund - Action Plan to support LGBTI+ Community Organisations
A Call for Applications was issued under Acton 6.3 National LGBTI+ Inclusion Strategy, by invitation to relevant stake-
holders. The 2024 Dormant Accounts Fund Action Plan includes the provision of €150,000 to support LGBTI+ Community 
Organisations and we await confirmation of the allocation for Waterford.  The closing date for receipt of applications is 
30th September 2024.
LEADER 2023-2027

The Business Pledge for a Cleaner, Greener Waterford – Deadline October 18th
Businesses with rates of less than €10,000 per annum, along with hospitality and leisure businesses, are setting out their 
plans to become more sustainable businesses through the Business Pledge for a Cleaner, Greener Waterford. Those 
who make the Pledge are eligible for a Rates discount of 9%. With almost 25% of greenhouse gas emissions coming from 
business in Waterford, the Council in 2021 decided to use its influence to help businesses save energy and reduce emis-
sions through a rates discount, allowing businesses to use the money saved to invest in energy efficiency. Businesses 
have until October 18th to apply. This is an opportunity that should not be missed, as our Business Pledge ambassadors 
like Dooley’s Hotel will tell you, going green for business saves money and attracts customers. 
Support for households on energy grants through the Community Energy Hub 
The Southeast Energy Agency in partnership with Waterford’s Library have developed a website called the Community 
Energy Hub. This website is a source of all of the information you might need to make energy improvements in your home. 
Also please note that if you would like printed information for your constituents the Climate Team have Energy Booklets 
that can be sent out to you. Please contact climateaction@waterfordcouncil.ie

The Control of Dogs (XL Bully Type Dog) Regulations 2024
From 1st October, 2024 new ownership rules are being introduced to protect public safety following a number of attacks 
by XL Bully type dogs.  
From 1st October 2024 the Control of Dogs (XL Bully Type Dog) Regulations 2024 will prohibit the importing, breeding, 
selling and re-homing of XL Bully type dogs.  From 1st February 2025 it will be illegal to own an XL Bully type dog without 
a ‘Certificate of Exemption’ issued by the local authority in which the dog resides.
XL Bully owners have between 1st October 2024 and 31st January 2025 to apply for a Certificate of Exemption.  A 
Certificate of Exemption is issued by the Local Authority and authorises the owner of an XL Bully type dog to keep that 
dog at a particular premises until the natural end of the dog’s life.
This certificate will be unique to each XL Bully type dog and owner, and will specify the dog’s licence details, microchip 
details, neutering details, age and description. It will also specify the dog owner’s name, address, date of birth and contact 
number. 
After 1st February 2025 all XL Bully type dog owners should either be in possession of a Certificate of Exemption or have 
proof that they applied for a Certificate of Exemption.  Owners may be required to present their Certificate of Exemption 
to a Dog Warden or a member of An Garda Síochána within 10 Days of a request to do so.
Any XL Bully types that are in pounds or rescues on or before 1st October 2024 may be rehomed.
Owners can apply, free of charge, to Waterford City & County Council from 1st October 2024 for a Certificate of Exemption 
through our website, through email or by post.   Further details are available on our website or at www.gov.ie/xlbully
